absent: Locking, concurrency, interrupt and sleep context rules for helpers and descriptors.
Full layout of struct usb_endpoint_descriptor and numeric values of number, direction and transfer type masks.
Endian conversion behavior, multiplier macro internals, and pointer validation beyond the null stream check.
Transition triggers, error recovery and timing for device and link state machines.
Allocation, lifetime, bounds checking and parsing rules for variable length tails.

findings.text: Provides small query operations over an endpoint descriptor that reveal its numeric index, its transfer category encoding, and whether its address indicates inbound or outbound direction. Callers supply a descriptor pointer and receive an integer interpretation of the masked field.

Provides four boolean style checks that report whether an endpoint uses bulk, control, interrupt or isochronous transfer. Each check examines the masked attribute portion and compares against the corresponding transfer encoding.

Provides six combined predicates that report bulk, interrupt or isochronous transfer together with inbound or outbound direction. Each combined check is true only when both the transfer category condition and the direction condition hold.

Provides packet size queries that convert the little endian size field to host order before masking, plus a multiplier query that derives a one based burst factor and an interrupt type query that isolates the interrupt classification portion from attributes.
Provides a stream count query over a SuperSpeed companion descriptor. A missing descriptor or a zero encoded value yields zero; otherwise the low five attribute bits select a power of two count.
Defines a packed eight octet isochronous companion layout with length and type bytes followed by a little endian packet size and a little endian bytes per interval count.
Defines a packed eight octet SuperSpeed Plus isochronous companion layout with length and type bytes, a reserved little endian word, and a little endian bytes per interval count.
Defines a packed six octet SuperSpeed companion layout with length, type, maximum burst and attribute bytes followed by a little endian bytes per interval value.

Defines small packed device level descriptors sharing a length plus type prefix: a qualifier with version, class triple, packet size, configuration count and reserved byte; single byte attribute OTG variants where the newer form adds a little endian OTG version; and a debug descriptor carrying inbound and outbound endpoint numbers.

Defines packed association and security descriptors with a common length plus type prefix. Association groups interfaces and function identity; security reports total length and encryption type count; key carries a three byte identifier plus variable key material; encryption reports type, value and key index; BOS reports total length and capability count.

Defines a three byte capability header with length, type and capability type fields, plus an eleven octet wireless capability that adds attributes, a little endian rate map, power info bytes, a little endian band group and a reserved byte.

Defines link power management capability layouts with a shared three byte header. The extended form adds a little endian attribute word; the SuperSpeed form adds attributes, a little endian speed map, a functionality byte and exit latency fields.

Defines larger capability layouts with a shared header. Container identity carries a sixteen byte identifier; platform capability carries a sixteen byte identifier plus variable data; SuperSpeed Plus capability carries attributes, functionality, reserved space and a trailing flexible list of sublink speed entries.

Defines power delivery capability layouts with a shared header. The main form carries attribute, port map and version fields; battery info carries string indexes, identifiers, thresholds and capacity values; consumer ports carry voltage, power and timing values; provider ports carry object count plus variable power objects.

Defines three small packed descriptors with a length plus type prefix: a minimal timing capability with only the shared header fields, an authentication capability with attribute, protocol and capability bytes, and a wireless endpoint companion with burst, sequence, delay, packet size, interval and compound attribute fields.

Defines fixed size security and power management records. Handshake carries message number, status, identifier, connection identifier, nonce and integrity fields; connection context carries three sixteen byte secrets; link timing request carries one byte and little endian two byte selection and exit values.

Specifies a device enumeration lifecycle from detached through attached, powered, authentication related reconnecting and unauthenticated phases, then default, addressed and configured functional states, with a suspended overlay that can return to the prior functional phase.
Specifies a four phase SuperSpeed link power progression from active operation through two intermediate low power phases to the deepest suspend phase.
Orders supported signalling rates from unknown during enumeration through low, full, high and wireless generations to SuperSpeed and SuperSpeed Plus generations.

Interrupt classification uses mask 0x30 with periodic and notification encodings; synchronization classification uses mask 0x0c with none, asynchronous, adaptive and synchronous encodings; usage classification uses mask 0x30 with data, feedback and implicit feedback encodings.
On the go capability flags occupy bit positions zero through three for session request, host negotiation, attach detection and remote signalling support, and status queries use selector value 0xF000.
Encryption selection uses values zero to three distinguishing unsecured operation, wired mode, a symmetric session mode and an asymmetric authentication mode.
Wireless capability encodes peer role, beacon behaviour over two bits with self, directed and absent variants, and eight physical rate presence bits spanning low to high throughput grades.

Extended capability reports link power management and latency tolerance support plus baseline and deep latency valid flags with four bit baseline and deep fields packed into one attribute word; SuperSpeed capability reports latency tolerance support and four operating speed presence bits.

SuperSpeed Plus capability packs sublink speed entry counts, minimum speed identity and lane counts, plus per entry speed identity, lane speed exponent with four magnitude grades, symmetric versus asymmetric direction type, reserved bits, link protocol selection and lane speed mantissa fields.

Device capability type identifiers assign wireless one, extended power management two, SuperSpeed three, container identity four, platform five, power delivery roles six through nine, SuperSpeed Plus ten, and timing eleven.

Nominal sizes use five octets for BOS, three for timing, seven for extended, ten for SuperSpeed, eleven for wireless, twenty for container, eight for association and both isochronous companions, and six for SuperSpeed companion, while platform adds payload length to a twenty octet base and SuperSpeed Plus adds four octets per entry to a twelve octet base.

Power delivery attributes flag battery charging, power delivery, provider, consumer, charging policy, Type C current and power source roles; consumer and provider port maps flag legacy, power delivery and Type C operation; unknown peak power duration uses an all ones timing value.

Burst scaling adds one to a two bit field; isochronous companion presence is tested via a high attribute bit; wireless companion switching uses a two bit selector with absent, switch and scale modes; link power uses disabled zero, maxima 0x7F and 0xFE, device initiated 0xFF, and selection limits 0xFF and 0xFFFF; self powered draw limit is 100.

All endpoint queries share masking then compare semantics over address or attribute bytes, combined predicates require both constituents, packet size extraction converts endian order before masking, and stream counts follow an all or power of two rule with zero for absent or zero encodings.

Every descriptor is tightly packed without padding, multi octet numeric fields use little endian order, and several descriptors end with flexible or variable length tails whose actual length must be derived from length or count fields rather than the static type.

Callers must handle absent companion pointers, zero stream encodings, reserved words and bytes that must be preserved but not interpreted, and trailing variable material that makes fixed size copies unsafe without consulting length fields.
